_comment: delegation/ORCHESTRATION.json — the run config for an autonomous build (D32). Copy into the consumer project's delegation/ folder and fill in. Read by scripts/orchestrate.mjs; also read by an auditor spawning workers natively. See prompts/AUTONOMOUS-BUILD.md Step 3.
_harness: Descriptive label only (claude-code | codex | generic ...). Which worker CLI actually runs is chosen by `adapter` below.
_adapter: The worker adapter to use for every task: one KEY of `adapters` below (claude-code, cline, opencode, codex, gemini, relay). A ledger column named `Adapter` overrides it per task. The name is only ever a lookup key in the `adapters` whitelist — it is never put on a command line — so a name not listed here is refused. Leave empty if your harness spawns subagents natively; then orchestrate.mjs is not used at all.

claude-code._note: Verified 2026-10-02 against `claude --help` (-p/--print, --permission-mode acceptEdits, --output-format json). Not run end to end by the kit's tests.

cline._note: Flags verified 2026-10-02 against `cline --help` (3.0.68): positional prompt, -c/--cwd, --json; auto-approve is the default. NOT run — it needs `cline auth` first. Add "--timeout", "1800" if you want a hard stop.

opencode._note: Flags verified 2026-10-02 against `opencode run --help` (1.18.34): positional message, --dir, --auto (approves permissions not explicitly denied — dangerous; remove it to be asked). Keep the message LAST and never use -f before it: -f takes an array and swallows the message. NOT run.

codex._note: UNVERIFIED here — codex is not installed on the machine that wrote this. Shape carried over from the kit's 2026-08-26 preset, minus the $(cat ...). Run `codex exec --help` and one task by hand first.

gemini._note: UNVERIFIED here — gemini is not installed on the machine that wrote this. Shape carried over from the kit's 2026-08-26 preset, minus the $(cat ...). Run `gemini --help` and one task by hand first.

relay._note: For a GUI or chat worker that has no CLI. orchestrate.mjs prints the PACKET.md path and waits for delegation/tasks/<id>/RESULT.json, then gives up with a clear message after timeoutSeconds. A relayed worker needs repo access (or the packet pasted whole) — the packet names absolute paths.

_adaptersHelp: Each adapter is {argv: [...]} — an ARGV ARRAY, run without a shell — or {type: "relay"}. argv placeholders: {{POINTER}} (a short "Read <PACKET.md> and follow it exactly" string), {{PACKET_FILE}}, {{PROJECT_ROOT}}, {{TASK_ID}}, {{NODE}} (this node binary). Optional: "stdin": "packet" | "pointer" feeds the packet text or the pointer on stdin instead of argv; "timeoutSeconds": N kills a worker that runs too long. Windows: npm-installed CLIs are .cmd shims; they are run through cmd.exe only when every argument is free of & % ^ ! and quotes, otherwise use `relay`. Before the first wave run ONE worker by hand on ONE task: a subtly wrong adapter fails identically for every task.
_workerCmd: LEGACY. A command line used only when `adapter` is empty. It is split into words and run WITHOUT a shell: quotes group words; |, &, ;, <, >, $(...) and backticks are refused. {{TASK_ID}}, {{POINTER}}, {{PACKET_FILE}} and {{PROJECT_ROOT}} are substituted ({{PROMPT_FILE}} is an alias for {{PACKET_FILE}}). Prefer `adapters`.

_workerCmdPresets._note: Verified 2026-10-02 against each installed tool's own --help; codex and gemini are not installed here and are unverified. These are the one-line shapes of the `adapters` entries above, for reading. Re-check before relying on them — this is exactly the kind of claim SPEC-AUTHOR.md's B-pass (check for rot) exists to catch.
_workerCmdPresets.relay: print PACKET.md path; wait for RESULT.json

_promptFile: Optional. A worker prompt to render the packet from instead of the kit's prompts/WORKER-SESSION.md (path relative to the project root, or inside the kit). A ledger column named `Prompt file` overrides it per task. It may use {{TASK_ID}}, {{TASK_BRIEF}}, {{TOUCHED_FILES}}, {{ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}}, {{INTERFACE_CONTRACT}}, {{TIER_POLICY}}, {{PROJECT_ROOT}}, {{KIT_ROOT}}, {{PACKET_FILE}}, {{RESULT_FILE}}; any other {{...}} stops the run.
_packets: Every dispatched task gets delegation/tasks/<id>/PACKET.md, rendered from its LEDGER row (Touched files), delegation/tasks/<id>/BRIEF.md (sections: Brief — or Context + Scope —, Acceptance criteria, Interface contract; the headings of templates/TASK-BRIEF.md work) and the worker prompt. A missing value stops the whole wave before anything is spawned. `node scripts/orchestrate.mjs --dry-run` shows which packets would render; `--render` writes them without spawning.
_remoteWorkers: For execution mode `auditor-remote` (D35) the auditor runs here and the workers run on another provider's CLI (or, with `relay`, in a GUI a human operates). Watch for capability asymmetry: a weaker worker model needs a tighter brief and a narrower task, and it fails subtly and confidently rather than loudly. For a genuinely hard task — a from-scratch algorithm, a security-sensitive path, a concurrency question — put that one on a frontier model at its highest reasoning setting.
_maxParallel: How many workers run at once. Start at 2-3. More contention than you expect comes from the gate, not the code.
_maxRetries: How many times a failing task is re-issued to a FRESH worker before it is marked failed. The auditor never patches worker output itself — that would make it both author and reviewer.
_tierPolicy: Which escalation tiers a worker may decide alone. T2 always stops and asks. Uncertainty resolves to T2, never T1 — see lib/patterns/tiered-escalation.md §1.2.
_haltOn: Conditions that stop the WHOLE run rather than parking one task. Keep this near-empty: a T2 parks its own task and its dependents, and everything else keeps building. Reasonable entries: 'gate-red-after-integration', 'repo-dirty-outside-task-scope'.
